_comment: Which Pro block attributes are COPY: text a reader or an editor sees, which a shipped pattern must offer for translation. Core's `role: "content"` is the editor's hint for content-only editing and pattern transforms, not a definition of copy (theme defect history, "Copy defined by core's role flag"), so every string attribute in an extension sidecar (inc/extensions/src/controls/*/attributes.json) and in a Pro block.json is classified here or carries the role. An attribute with the role needs no entry: the theme's capture and i18n gate read the role from the editor's and the server's block registries. `copy` lists copy WITHOUT the role, each with the reason the role is wrong for it; the theme's tools/lib/i18n-targets.mjs must name each one in BLOCK_COPY_ATTRIBUTES (and each `nested_copy` path), or capture ships it as a raw English literal. `not_copy` lists everything else, grouped by why. inc/extensions/src/copy-attributes.test.js fails an unclassified string attribute, a stale or doubled key, and a listed attribute that carries the role.

copy.why: The menu button's visible label. No role: core/navigation is already a content block (supports.contentRole), and a role here would make pattern transforms keep this one attribute and drop the navigation's ref and every other setting (getRetainedBlockAttributes keeps only content-role attributes).
The item's description line under its label. Core gives the navigation-submenu and navigation-link description no role either; the label carries it.
The link's title attribute, as on core's navigation-link and navigation-submenu, which carry no role for it.

The form's name in the submissions screen and the notification email. No role on any blocklane/form attribute: form-contact declares blockTypes blocklane/form, and a role would make that pattern transform drop the form's id, recipients and settings.
The notification email's subject line. No role, for the pattern-transform reason on formName.
The message a visitor reads when the form is closed. No role, for the pattern-transform reason on formName.
The message a visitor reads on a duplicate submission. No role, for the pattern-transform reason on formName.

nested_copy.why: The auto-reply's subject line, which the visitor reads.
The auto-reply's body, which the visitor reads.

not_copy.why: A URL, a link target or a link kind.
A CSS length, a preset reference or a color value.
A choice from a fixed set of tokens the code reads, never shown as text.
SVG markup, drawn and never read as text.
What the form submits or checks: a field name, a submitted value, a prefill a hidden field uses as a token, a bound, an id, an address list or a date. Translating it changes what the form sends.
